title: Generative Thinking, Corrective Action: User-Friendly Composed Image Retrieval via Automatic Multi-Agent Collaboration

problem.claim: Zero-shot composed image retrieval aims to retrieve images matching a reference image and textual description without training on triplet datasets.

gap.claim: Existing fixed, hand-crafted retrieval processes produce non-adaptive queries and user-unfriendly retrieval interactions.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes AutoCIR, an automatic multi-agent collaboration framework for zero-shot composed image retrieval.
AutoCIR uses three training-free agents—a planner, retriever, and corrector—to iteratively identify and rectify mismatches.
The planner generates and refines customized target captions, while the corrector evaluates retrieved results and generates self-correction actions using chain-of-thought reasoning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe AutoCIR as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three benchmarks reportedly show that AutoCIR consistently outperforms previous competitive methods for zero-shot composed image retrieval.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines zero-shot composed image retrieval as matching a composed image-text query without triplet-dataset training.
Identifies non-adaptive queries and user-unfriendly processes in existing fixed retrieval methods.
Describes caption planning and refinement, retrieval-result evaluation, and self-correction.
Reports consistent outperformance on three benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates query planning, retrieval, and correction into collaborating agents.

interpretation.claim: Explicit role separation may support adaptive retrieval and iterative error correction.

application.claim: For multimodal retrieval workflows, consider decomposing query construction, result evaluation, and correction into coordinated stages.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which agent, interaction, or benchmark condition accounts for the reported improvement.

unknowns: Benchmark names, metrics, dataset sizes, and quantitative results are not provided.
The abstract does not specify implementation details, baseline configurations, or limitations.
